units.title: Vasodilator Classification and Calcium Channel Blocker Comparison
units.sec: Vasodilator Classification and Calcium Channel Blocker Comparison · p83
units.guide: Vasodilators are classified by hemodynamic target: arterial dilators lower afterload, venodilators lower preload and sodium nitroprusside is mixed. Calcium channel blockers split into non-DHP diltiazem/verapamil and DHP agents. Non-DHP agents are weaker vasodilators but late AV/SA nodal blockers used in arrhythmia, whereas DHPs are potent vasodilators with significant reflex tachycardia and no AV nodal block.

units.title: Calcium Channel Blocker Adverse Effects and Uses
units.sec: Calcium Channel Blocker Adverse Effects and Uses · p84
units.guide: Calcium channel blockers are first-line antihypertensives and DOC for Raynaud phenomenon; oral nimodipine prevents cerebral vasoconstriction after subarachnoid hemorrhage because it is lipid soluble and crosses the BBB. Their adverse effects reflect vasodilation and nodal block: headache is most common, amlodipine causes precapillary ankle edema prevented by low-dose amlodipine plus ACEI, verapamil causes constipation, and diltiazem/verapamil cannot be combined with β blockers.

units.title: Other Arterial Dilators: Hydralazine, Minoxidil, Diazoxide and Fenoldopam
units.sec: Other Arterial Dilators: Hydralazine, Minoxidil, Diazoxide and Fenoldopam · p84
units.guide: Hydralazine blocks IP3-induced Ca2+ channels, opens K+ channels and increases NO; it is used for hypertensive emergency in pregnancy, though IV labetalol is the DOC, and can cause SLE/Sweet syndrome. Minoxidil is a potent K+ opener used orally as a second-line elderly antihypertensive and topically in androgenic alopecia; diazoxide is for insulinoma but can cause shock; fenoldopam is a D1 and α2 agonist.

units.title: Nitroglycerin Mechanism, Uses, Tolerance and Contraindications
units.sec: Nitroglycerin Mechanism, Uses, Tolerance and Contraindications · p85
units.guide: Nitroglycerin is converted by aldehyde dehydrogenase to nitric oxide, which stimulates guanylate cyclase to raise cGMP and relax smooth muscle. cGMP is metabolized by PDE5, so sildenafil/tadalafil interact dangerously with nitrates. NTG is DOC sublingually for acute angina, patch/gel for prophylaxis, useful for MI pain and esophageal spasm, but causes tolerance prevented by an 8-hour nitrate-free nighttime interval and causes headache/Monday disease/postural hypotension.

units.title: Isosorbide Nitrates and Sodium Nitroprusside
units.sec: Isosorbide Nitrates and Sodium Nitroprusside · p86
units.guide: Isosorbide dinitrate is an oral nitrate that undergoes first-pass denitration to active isosorbide mononitrate; IDN is used orally for angina prophylaxis and sublingually for acute angina. Isosorbide mononitrate has 0% first-pass metabolism and is used orally for long-term prophylaxis. Sodium nitroprusside is a mixed dilator metabolized to therapeutic NO and toxic cyanide/thiocyanate, so it is not preferred for hypertensive emergency/aortic dissection despite being effective.

units.title: RAAS Physiology, ACE Inhibition and Contraindications
units.sec: RAAS Physiology, ACE Inhibition and Contraindications · p87
units.guide: The RAAS page maps liver angiotensinogen to angiotensin I through kidney renin, then lung ACE to angiotensin II, then aminopeptidases to angiotensin III and IV. ACE also behaves like kininase, so ACE inhibitors increase bradykinin, prostaglandins and substance P, causing dry cough and angioedema. Angiotensin II/III act through AT1 receptors on vessels, adrenals and glomeruli; RAAS blockers cause postural hypotension/hyperkalemia and are contraindicated in pregnancy and bilateral renal artery stenosis.

units.title: ACE Inhibitors, ARBs, Aliskiren and Captopril Test
units.sec: ACE Inhibitors, ARBs, Aliskiren and Captopril Test · p88
units.guide: The drug table gives ACE inhibitors, ARBs and direct renin inhibitors. ACE inhibitors include captopril, lisinopril, fosinopril, enalapril and IV enalaprilat; ARBs include losartan with PPARγ/uricosuric/TXA2 effects, telmisartan as the maximum PPARγ agonist, olmesartan and irbesartan with AV nodal AF rate control; aliskiren is the direct renin inhibitor. ACEI/ARBs are first-line for hyperreninemic HTN and DOC in HTN with DM, CKD, nephrotic syndrome and scleroderma; captopril testing differentiates renovascular from essential hypertension.
